record.original_question: Let F: Ω → P_0(X) be a multifunction from a complete probability space into the nonempty subsets of a Banach space X. If F has convex closed values and is scalarly measurable, meaning F^{-}(H) is measurable for every open half-space H ⊆ X, must F admit a selector f: Ω → X that is itself scalarly measurable?

evidence.quote: Problem 2.7. Let F: Ω → P_0(X) be a scalarly measurable multi-function with convex closed values. Does F admit scalarly measurable selectors?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $(\Omega, \Sigma, \mu)$ be a complete probability space and let $X$ be a (real) Banach space with topological dual $X^{*}$. Denote by $\mathcal{P}_{0}(X)$ the family of all nonempty subsets of $X$. A multifunction $F : \Omega \to \mathcal{P}_{0}(X)$ is said to be scalarly measurable if, for every $x^{*} \in X^{*}$, the support function
$$\omega \mapsto \delta^{*}(x^{*}, F(\omega)) := \sup_{x \in F(\omega)} \langle x^{*}, x \rangle$$
is $\Sigma$-measurable; equivalently, $F^{-}(H) := \{\omega \in \Omega : F(\omega) \cap H \neq \emptyset\} \in \Sigma$ for every open half-space $H \subseteq X$. A selector of $F$ is a function $f : \Omega \to X$ with $f(\omega) \in F(\omega)$ for every $\omega \in \Omega$; $f$ is called scalarly measurable if $\omega \mapsto \langle x^{*}, f(\omega) \rangle$ is measurable for every $x^{*} \in X^{*}$.

Question: Suppose $F : \Omega \to \mathcal{P}_{0}(X)$ is scalarly measurable and has convex, norm-closed values. Must $F$ admit a scalarly measurable selector?
artifact.category_tag: Measurable selectors of multifunctions in Banach spaces
artifact.status_search_result: Positive answers are known in significant special cases — for instance, scalarly measurable multifunctions with weakly compact (not necessarily convex) values in arbitrary Banach spaces admit scalarly measurable selectors, and various separable or property-(P)-type settings give selector theorems. However, the general case of convex norm-closed values in an arbitrary Banach space does not appear to be definitively settled in the located literature; subsequent work on selections of integrable multifunctions in arbitrary Banach spaces continues to investigate variants of this question.

status_evidence.title: Measurability and Selections of Multi-Functions in Banach Spaces (Cascales, Rodríguez)
status_evidence.snippet: Selection theorems for scalarly measurable multifunctions are obtained under property (P) and weak compactness assumptions on the values.
status_evidence.claim: Selector theorems known for weakly compact values and under additional properties, leaving the general convex-closed case as a problem.

status_evidence.title: Pettis Integrability of Multifunctions with Values in Arbitrary Banach Spaces
status_evidence.snippet: Each scalarly measurable multifunction taking weakly compact values in a general Banach space possesses scalarly measurable selections.
status_evidence.claim: Affirmative answer for weakly compact values in arbitrary Banach spaces.

status_evidence.title: Selections of Integrable Multifunctions in Arbitrary Banach Spaces (Di Piazza, Sambucini, 2025)
status_evidence.snippet: Recent work continues to study selection problems for multifunctions in arbitrary (possibly non-separable) Banach spaces.
status_evidence.claim: Continued research indicates that selector questions for multifunctions in arbitrary Banach spaces remain an active topic.
